mustRecognize: Manufacturer, field-strength and software-version heterogeneity are explicit scientific comparability dimensions.
The intended comparison is between a disease population and a reference population.
A central Core Lab is planned, while its operational realization remains unresolved.
Acquisition harmonization, QC, reader organization and analysis are unresolved.
Equipment provenance and metadata are required to assess robustness and comparability.
mustPreserve: Prospective multicenter scope and the explicit sources of technical heterogeneity.
The Core Lab principle without fabricating its procedures.
Uncertainty about interchangeability, harmonization, QC, readers and analysis.
Project/source provenance and document commitment boundaries.
mustConsider: Site/scanner qualification and acquisition harmonization alternatives.
QC, reader variability, central reading and adjudication implications.
Measurement validity, robustness and heterogeneity-aware analysis.
Equipment, software, acquisition and derivation metadata requirements.
Protocol versus Imaging Charter/Core Lab Manual detail allocation.
mustNotInvent: Scanner compatibility or interchangeability across manufacturers or field strengths.
A specific sequence parameter set, correction method or harmonization algorithm.
Reader count, qualification thresholds, QC limits or Core Lab procedures.
Evidence-backed documentary detail where only a pattern or metadata exists.
mustNotDo: Confuse a Core Lab principle with a complete operational workflow.
Force unsupported specialized-manual details into the Protocol.
Treat DOC-002R patterns as universal laws or as Project truth.
acceptableAlternativeFamilies: Centralized, distributed or hybrid reading candidates with explicit comparability controls.
Prospective harmonization, calibration/bridging, stratification or model-based heterogeneity strategies when evidence supports them.
Different document allocations consistent with commitment level and operational ownership.
Alternative disease/reference comparison and robustness frameworks subject to human adoption.
requiredOwnershipBoundaries: Imaging addresses acquisition, equipment and Core Lab mechanics without adopting scientific endpoints.
OBS addresses measurement validity/robustness; Biostatistics addresses conditional analyses.
CDM/Data Management represent adopted metadata and flows without deciding scientific acceptability.
QRY selects the next action; Knowledge and DOC-002R remain evidence/context, not decision owners.
requiredEvidenceBehavior: Equipment and comparability claims preserve source identity and applicability limits.
Unavailable or rights-restricted platform content is not reconstructed.
Documentary patterns are applied as contextual evidence, with justified divergence permitted.
requiredHumanBoundaries: Human adoption of population/objective and measurement strategy.
Human adoption of harmonization, QC, reader/Core Lab and analytic strategies.
Human adjudication of professionally context-dependent documentary detail.
documentaryExpectations: Protocol contains appropriate commitments, not unsupported operational detail.
Imaging Charter/Core Lab Manual needs and boundaries are surfaced where material.
Cross-document equipment, QC, reader and analysis statements remain versioned and Project-faithful.
blockingFailureConditions: Explicit technical heterogeneity or Core Lab uncertainty is materially lost.
Equipment equivalence, acquisition parameters, reader organization or QC limits are invented.
Document detail is allocated in a way that materially misstates Project commitments.
Owner reachability, Project provenance or first-divergence reconstruction fails.
nonBlockingFindingExamples: A secondary harmonization option is omitted.
A specialized manual could contain more professional detail without changing Protocol fidelity.
